ellen_customer: Hey team — since the canary push of rwd/gpt-2.1 ~18:30 UTC our function calls to our payment tool are failing with schema errors. Happening only when requests are routed to the new model. Sample req id: req-9f8a7c. Latency also up ~300ms for these flows. Can someone escalate?

alice_support: Sorry about that, @ellen_customer. Can you paste the raw request payload + the response you got from the API? We'll grab the routing logs and escalate to eng.

ellen_customer: Pasting the client-side payload and the API response we saw (mangled IDs shortened):

```json
{ 
  "id": "req-9f8a7c",
  "model": "rwd/gpt-2.1",
  "input": "charge user",
  "tool_call": {
    "name": "payment-charge",
    "arguments": { "amount": 100, "currency": "USD", "customer_id": "cus_123" }
  }
}
```

API response (status 400):

```json
{
  "error": "tool_call_schema_validation_failed",
  "details": "missing required field: value_cents",
  "tool_response_id": "tr-77a"
}
```

And from our server logs showing the runtime decision paths: 
```
[2026-03-17T18:30:12Z] request=req-9f8a7c routed_model=rwd/gpt-2.1
[2026-03-17T18:30:12Z] request=req-9f8a7c model_response: chosen_tool=charge_payment_v3 args=\"{\"value\":\"100\",\"cur\":\"USD\"}\"
[2026-03-17T18:30:12Z] runtime: validating args against charge_payment_v3 schema -> missing value_cents
```
This looks like the model switched to a different tool variant (charge_payment_v3) and returned different arg names/types. Not an issue pre-canary.

ben_oncall: @alice_support thanks. @carla_eng fyi — that log line makes it look like the model is choosing a different tool name and returning an args object that doesn't match the registered schema for that tool. Can you check the model-tool mapping / function registry? Also please attach route config (are we allowing model-specific tool aliases?). :eyes:

carla_eng: I'm pulling the canary routing config now. Two quick checks: (1) did we ship any function spec changes with the model onboarding? (2) did the canary include a model alias mapping change?

alice_support: No function spec changes in the last 24h from the customer side. @deploy-bot can you show the canary promotion event for rwd/gpt-2.1?

deploy-bot: Canary promoted: rwd/gpt-2.1 -> canary (deploy id: dpl-884). Owner: infra-release. Time: 2026-03-17T18:15:00Z.

ben_oncall: OK — likely regression introduced by the model's tool-selection behavior. Two immediate options: (A) rollback canary to previous model (restore routing) so production callers see previous behavior, or (B) patch runtime to map charge_payment_v3 -> payment-charge schema (quick shim). Which do we prefer?

dave_product: From product standpoint we should rollback the canary until we have a deterministic fix. Risk of incorrect charges is high. Please roll back canary and open a follow-up with root cause and patch ETA.

carla_eng: Initiating rollback now. I'll also collect full model decision traces to confirm whether the model invented v3 or we accidentally registered an alias mapping.

[2026-03-17T18:34:05Z] deploy-bot: Rollback executed: rwd/gpt-2.1 removed from canary routing (rollback id rb-332). Previous model restored for canary traffic.

alice_support: @ellen_customer can you confirm if your failing requests are succeeding again? Also we'll keep monitoring latency.

ellen_customer: Confirmed — after the rollback our function calls succeed again. No more schema errors and latency back to normal. Thanks for the quick action. :relieved:

ben_oncall: Thanks. We're collecting decision traces for all affected reqs (req-9f8a7c + a batch of similar ids) and will attach them to the ticket. Early hypothesis: model returns an unregistered tool name with a different argument schema. Could be a model packaging/metadata mismatch during onboarding.

carla_eng: Collected traces and the model_response shows the token-level generation for the tool call. It's consistent: rwd/gpt-2.1 prefers `charge_payment_v3` in these utterances. No runtime aliasing change found in the last deploy. So it's model-driven.

alice_support: Created support ticket INC-2026-881 and attached traces, sample payloads, and deploy IDs. Assigned to eng oncall and research.

dave_product: Please schedule a postmortem with research and model onboarding — we need a checklist for models that include tool names to avoid these mismatches. Also consider adding a runtime safety rule: reject tool names that aren't an exact registered function name instead of attempting auto-wrapping.

ben_oncall: Agreed. Short term: add a runtime guard so unrecognized tool names are treated as a soft-fail and fall back to previous model variant. Longer term: update model onboarding to require explicit tool-name-to-function mapping in the manifest.

ellen_customer: Appreciate the quick rollback and the follow-up plans. Please keep me posted on ETA for the guard/patch — we depend on toolcalls for billing flows.

alice_support: Will do. I'll DM you updates and link INC-2026-881 here when we have a timeline.

carla_eng: Marking this thread for postmortem. Closing the immediate canary incident.

ellen_customer: Thanks everyone.
